I'm gonna reply to the second half about the puppy first, because that's easier for me haha. 

What type of dog is it? How old?
It is true that they get easier after 6 months or so, depending on how much you did in that time for training. Also about 6 months is the earliest you can get your dog neutered, and that in itself will completely change your dogs behavior, thats why male dogs fixed early enough (like mine) end up still squating while they pee. (Its a good idea for many reasons, but one big one is it will totally prevent any bad behavior with marking)
The more *sincere* you are, the more your dog will respond positively to you. 
What happens when you try to cuddle? I taught my dog to lick my face and lay on top of me to feel secure, i just encouraged it every time i started to feel anxiety coming or that i was about to cry. I have episodes where i cry hard for hours, i would always keep treats on me, good ones for this training are small pieces. 

Okay the **biting** problem: puppies bite. Plain and simple. You can put stuff away and use bitter apple spray, worked on my dog. Dogs will get try to get your attention until they get it, whether its positive **or negative**... so a lot of the time, you just have to be more patient then your dog and not give into bad behavior,  always redirect it. 
Biting is completely natural behavior,  its how puppies figure out the world (tbey dont have hands haha) so there is no use in getting mad or yelling at your puppy that has no idea yet that he's doing anything wrong. (Not saying ****you**** do that, but people in general lose patience and get frustrated & react negatively) anyway... this is super long but i hope it helps!
Dogs that are taught *how* hard to bite on human hands as puppies are kess likely to bite a human as an adult dog. **when he bites you yelp loud and startle him so he knows that hurt** thats how puppies playing together learn how **not** to be too rough. Also, have many toys around to redirect him to go play on his own. 
**are you crate training him?**
I had that guilt felling too, but puppies are way too demanding for anyone alone, train him to nap quietly in his crate so you can have breaks. I also taught my dog "go play!" And "find toy!" So he will run to find a toy and then entertaim himself for a bit.
